items.summary: 本期时间轴制作：佟和看完《理想的存档》，我们几个没忍住，顺着片里熟悉的面孔聊起了旧事。聊陈星汉在接机路上掏出手机展示游戏原型，聊去波兰拍 CDPR 时的一路小插曲，也聊《黑神话》首次公开前，我们那阵手忙脚乱的对接。游戏圈这十年的变化，落在我们的记忆里，常常是一碗面、一趟车，或者一句“这事你怎么也记得”。这期就一起翻翻这些小事，看看当年的朋友们，后来把游戏做成了什么样。《理想的存档》由 TapTap 出品、机核 GSENSE 即视制作。 <《理想的存档》，中国游戏人亲述十年>

ja.title: 雨の中、空港で陳星漢さんを迎えに行き、カードマネージャーを探すために真夜中に車を停める｜過去10年間の私たちの断片
ja.summary: この号のタイムライン制作: トン・ヘさんが「アイデア アーカイブ」を観た後、私たちは映画に登場するおなじみの顔たちと昔のことについて話さずにはいられませんでした。私たちは、チェン・シンハンが空港に向かう途中で携帯電話を取り出してゲームのプロトタイプを見せたこと、彼がCDPRの撮影のためにポーランドに行ったときの出来事、そして「Black Myth」の最初のリリース前の私たちの必死のコミュニケーションについて話しました。過去 10 年間のゲーム業界の変化は、一杯の麺やバスに乗ったとき、あるいは「どうやってこれを覚えているの?」という文章とともに私たちの記憶に刻まれることがよくあります。今回は、これらの小さなことを一緒に見て、当時の友人たちがゲームで何をしたかを見てみましょう。 「Ideal Archive」はTapTapが制作し、GSENSEがプロデュースしています。 <中国人ゲーマーの過去10年間の個人記録「理想のアーカイブ」>

en.title: Picking up Chen Xinghan at the airport in the rain, parking the car in the middle of the night to find the card manager｜The fragments of us in the past ten years
en.summary: Timeline production of this issue: After Tong He watched "Ideal Archive", we couldn't help but chatted about old things with the familiar faces in the film. We talked about Chen Xinghan taking out his mobile phone to show the game prototype on the way to the airport, about the incident when he went to Poland to shoot CDPR, and about our frantic communication before the first release of "Black Myth". The changes in the gaming industry in the past ten years are often engraved in our memories with a bowl of noodles, a ride on the bus, or the sentence "How can you remember this?" In this issue, let’s look through these little things together and see what our friends from back then have done with the game. "Ideal Archive" is produced by TapTap and produced by GSENSE. <"Ideal Archive", a Chinese gamer's personal account of the past ten years>

en.title: Are Silicon Valley giants sincere in calling for AI to slow down? Can you lose weight?
en.summary: Recently, Anthropic CEO Amodei called for slowing down the iteration speed of cutting-edge large models to deal with potential AI security risks. The top closed-source AI laboratories in Silicon Valley responded collectively, triggering a wave of public opinion discussing the slowdown of AI. But while publicly calling for the brakes to be applied, while continuing to increase investment in computing power and technology, is this statement out of genuine concerns about the future of mankind, or is it a discourse strategy in the context of business competition and regulatory games? Can the idea of ​​slowing down the economy be implemented in reality? In this episode, Assistant Professor Huang Jingyang of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (Shenzhen) will trace the origins of the "speed-up theory", analyze the differences in the positions of various parties in the U.S. technology circle, and dismantle the current split between the two parties, the federal government, and local governments in the United States on AI regulation. Through the fog of acceleration and deceleration discourse, we also tried to clarify what the "technological theology" and worldview of Silicon Valley technology giants look like and how they were formed. Because this is something created by human beings who burn their souls with all their strength, and it will inevitably release a powerful and lasting light. Go home, it is the glory of the human soul! ■ Domestic EVA In the process of enjoying "Memory Authority", it is difficult for me not to think of "Neon Genesis Evangelion" (hereinafter abbreviated as "EVA").
